699	func (p *ProjectRunner) StartProcess(name string) error {
700		proc := p.getRunningProcess(name)
701		if proc != nil {
702			log.Error().Msgf("Process %s is already running", name)
703			return fmt.Errorf("process %s is already running", name)
704		}
705		if processConfig, ok := p.project.Processes[name]; ok {
706			p.runProcess(&processConfig)
707			// Resume schedule if it was paused (e.g. initially disabled)
708			if s := p.processScheduler.Load(); s != nil && s.IsScheduled(name) {
709				if err := s.ResumeProcess(name); err != nil {
710					log.Error().Err(err).Msgf("Failed to resume schedule for process %s", name)
711				}
712			}
713			// Resume an existing registration - a stopped process's watch is paused,
714			// not removed, so resuming it avoids re-walking the whole tree. A
715			// process with no registration becomes watchable only now: it may have
716			// been deferred (disabled, or excluded from an `up <process>...`
717			// selection) when the watcher was first populated.
718			if p.isProcessWatchRegistered(name) {
719				p.watchResume(name)
720			} else {
721				p.watchAdd(&processConfig)
722			}
723		} else {
724			return fmt.Errorf("no such process: %s", name)
725		}
726	
727		return nil
728	}
729	
730	func (p *ProjectRunner) StopProcess(name string) error {
731		log.Info().Msgf("Stopping %s", name)
732		// Claim the stop before touching the process: if a restart is between
733		// tearing the old incarnation down and starting its replacement, the
734		// shutdown below has nothing left to stop, and only this marker keeps the
735		// restart from undoing the stop.
736		p.noteStopRequest(name)
737		proc := p.getRunningProcess(name)
738	
739		var err error
740		if proc != nil {
741			err = proc.shutDownNoRestart()
742			if err != nil {
743				log.Err(err).Msgf("failed to stop process %s", name)
744			}
745		} else {
746			// A process that is not running may still be armed to start again on
747			// its own - by a schedule, or by a file watch. Stopping it then means
748			// disarming it, which is a perfectly sensible request and not an error:
749			// a process reading Scheduled or Watching is exactly what the user is
750			// looking at when they ask for it to stop.
751			// A process caught between the teardown and the relaunch of a restart
752			// is not "not running" either - the request that just landed is what
753			// keeps its replacement from starting, which is as real a stop as any.
754			sched := p.processScheduler.Load()
755			isScheduled := sched != nil && sched.IsScheduled(name)
756			if !isScheduled && !p.isProcessWatched(name) && !p.isRestartInFlight(name) {
757				if _, ok := p.project.Processes[name]; !ok {
758					log.Error().Msgf("Process %s does not exist", name)
759					return fmt.Errorf("process %s does not exist", name)
760				}
761				log.Error().Msgf("Process %s is not running", name)
762				return fmt.Errorf("process %s is not running", name)
763			}
764		}
765	
766		// A deliberately stopped process must not be brought back by a file change.
767		p.watchPause(name)
768	
769		// Pause schedule if it was running or scheduled
770		if sched := p.processScheduler.Load(); sched != nil && sched.IsScheduled(name) {
771			if pauseErr := sched.PauseProcess(name); pauseErr != nil {
772				log.Error().Err(pauseErr).Msgf("Failed to pause schedule for process %s", name)
773				if err == nil {
774					err = pauseErr
775				}
776			}
777		}
778	
779		return err
780	}

782	func (p *ProjectRunner) SendSignal(name string, sig int) error {
783		log.Info().Msgf("Sending signal %d to %s", sig, name)
784		proc := p.getRunningProcess(name)
785		if proc == nil {
786			if _, ok := p.project.Processes[name]; !ok {
787				log.Error().Msgf("Process %s does not exist", name)
788				return fmt.Errorf("process %s does not exist", name)
789			}
790			log.Error().Msgf("Process %s is not running", name)

package app

import (
	"runtime"
	"syscall"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/f1bonacc1/process-compose/src/command"
	"github.com/f1bonacc1/process-compose/src/types"
)

// Regression test for https://github.com/F1bonacc1/process-compose/issues/589
//
// A process can exit on the stop signal before the shutdown timeout starts
// waiting for it. The wait must still see that exit, instead of running out the
// timeout and then failing to SIGKILL the already-reaped PID.
func TestStopExitBeforeShutdownWait(t *testing.T) {
	if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
		t.Skip("relies on Unix signals")
	}
	const name = "worker"
	shell := command.DefaultShellConfig()

	runner, err := NewProjectRunner(&ProjectOpts{
		project: &types.Project{
			ShellConfig: shell,
			Processes: map[string]types.ProcessConfig{
				name: {
					Name:        name,
					ReplicaName: name,
					Executable:  shell.ShellCommand,
					Args:        []string{shell.ShellArgument, getSleepCommand(60.0)},
					ShutDownParams: types.ShutDownParams{
						Signal:          int(syscall.SIGTERM),
						ShutDownTimeout: 1,
					},
				},
			},
		},
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	go func() { _ = runner.Run() }()
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = runner.ShutDownProject() })

	waitForProcessState(t, runner, name, types.ProcessStateRunning, 10*time.Second)
	proc := runner.getRunningProcess(name)
	if proc == nil {
		t.Fatalf("process %s is not running", name)
	}

	// Replay the losing interleaving: the stop signal is sent and the process
	// exits and is reaped before the shutdown wait is set up.
	proc.setState(types.ProcessStateTerminating)
	if err := proc.command.Stop(int(syscall.SIGTERM), false); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("send SIGTERM: %v", err)
	}
	select {
	case <-proc.procDoneChan:
	case <-time.After(10 * time.Second):
		t.Fatalf("process %s did not exit on SIGTERM", name)
	}

	start := time.Now()
	if err := proc.forceKillOnTimeout(); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("forceKillOnTimeout after exit: %v", err)
	}
	if elapsed := time.Since(start); elapsed >= time.Second {
		t.Errorf("forceKillOnTimeout waited %v for a process that had already exited", elapsed)
	}
}

## Project Overview

Process Compose is a process orchestrator for non-containerized applications, written in Go. It uses YAML configuration (similar to docker-compose) to define and manage processes with dependency tracking, health checks, scheduling, and more. It operates in multiple modes: TUI (default), HTTP API server, daemon, and MCP server.

## Build & Development Commands

```bash
make build              # Build binary to bin/process-compose (CGO_ENABLED=0)
make test               # Run tests with coverage
make testrace           # Run tests with race detector
make testrace-clean     # Clear test cache, then run with race detector
make lint               # Run golangci-lint (downloads to ./bin/ if needed)
make coverhtml          # Generate HTML coverage report
make swag               # Regenerate Swagger/OpenAPI docs
make schema             # Regenerate JSON schema
make docs               # Regenerate CLI documentation
```

**Run a single test:**
```bash
go test -run TestName ./src/package/...
```

**Run with debug mode:**
```bash
PC_DEBUG_MODE=1 ./bin/process-compose -e .env
```

## Architecture

**Entry point:** `main.go` → `src/cmd/root.go` (Cobra CLI framework)

### Key Packages (all under `src/`)

| Package | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `cmd/` | Cobra CLI command definitions |
| `app/` | Core process execution engine — `ProjectRunner` manages lifecycle of all processes, `Process` wraps individual process execution |
| `types/` | Domain models — `Project`, `ProcessConfig`, `ProcessState`, dependency graph |
| `loader/` | YAML config parsing, env var expansion, project merging, validation |
| `config/` | CLI flags, global settings, themes, version info (embedded via ldflags) |
| `api/` | REST API using Gin framework, WebSocket support, Swagger docs |
| `tui/` | Terminal UI using `rivo/tview` — process table, log viewer, terminal view |
| `client/` | HTTP client for remote API communication |
| `health/` | Liveness/readiness probe implementations (HTTP, exec) |
| `scheduler/` | Cron/interval-based process scheduling via `gocron/v2` |

					Executable:  shell.ShellCommand,
					Args:        []string{shell.ShellArgument, getSleepCommand(60.0)},
					ShutDownParams: types.ShutDownParams{

						ShutDownTimeout: 1,
					},
				},
			},
		},
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	go func() { _ = runner.Run() }()
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = runner.ShutDownProject() })

	waitForProcessState(t, runner, name, types.ProcessStateRunning, 10*time.Second)
	proc := runner.getRunningProcess(name)
	if proc == nil {
		t.Fatalf("process %s is not running", name)
	}

	// Replay the losing interleaving: the stop signal is sent and the process
	// exits and is reaped before the shutdown wait is set up.
	proc.setState(types.ProcessStateTerminating)
	if err := proc.command.Stop(int(syscall.SIGTERM), false); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("send SIGTERM: %v", err)
	}
	select {
	case <-proc.procDoneChan:
	case <-time.After(10 * time.Second):
		t.Fatalf("process %s did not exit on SIGTERM", name)
	}

	start := time.Now()
	if err := proc.forceKillOnTimeout(); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("forceKillOnTimeout after exit: %v", err)
	}
	if elapsed := time.Since(start); elapsed >= time.Second {
		t.Errorf("forceKillOnTimeout waited %v for a process that had already exited", elapsed)
	}
}

# AGENTS.md

This file provides guidance to Codex (Codex.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

Process Compose is a process orchestrator for non-containerized applications, written in Go. It uses YAML configuration (similar to docker-compose) to define and manage processes with dependency tracking, health checks, scheduling, and more. It operates in multiple modes: TUI (default), HTTP API server, daemon, and MCP server.

## Build & Development Commands

```bash
make build              # Build binary to bin/process-compose (CGO_ENABLED=0)
make test               # Run tests with coverage
make testrace           # Run tests with race detector
make testrace-clean     # Clear test cache, then run with race detector
make lint               # Run golangci-lint (downloads to ./bin/ if needed)
make coverhtml          # Generate HTML coverage report
make swag               # Regenerate Swagger/OpenAPI docs
make schema             # Regenerate JSON schema
make docs               # Regenerate CLI documentation
```

**Run a single test:**
```bash
go test -run TestName ./src/package/...
```

**Run with debug mode:**
```bash
PC_DEBUG_MODE=1 ./bin/process-compose -e .env
```

## Architecture

**Entry point:** `main.go` → `src/cmd/root.go` (Cobra CLI framework)

### Key Packages (all under `src/`)

| Package | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `cmd/` | Cobra CLI command definitions |
| `app/` | Core process execution engine — `ProjectRunner` manages lifecycle of all processes, `Process` wraps individual process execution |
| `types/` | Domain models — `Project`, `ProcessConfig`, `ProcessState`, dependency graph |
| `loader/` | YAML config parsing, env var expansion, project merging, validation |
| `config/` | CLI flags, global settings, themes, version info (embedded via ldflags) |
| `api/` | REST API using Gin framework, WebSocket support, Swagger docs |
| `tui/` | Terminal UI using `rivo/tview` — process table, log viewer, terminal view |
| `client/` | HTTP client for remote API communication |
| `health/` | Liveness/readiness probe implementations (HTTP, exec) |
| `scheduler/` | Cron/interval-based process scheduling via `gocron/v2` |

## Termination Parameters

```yaml
processes:
  nginx:
    command: "docker run --rm --name nginx_test nginx"
    shutdown:
      command: "docker stop nginx_test"
      timeout_seconds: 10 # default 10
      signal: 15 # default 15, but only if the 'command' is not defined or empty
      parent_only: no  # default no. If yes, only signal the running process instead of its whole process group
```

`shutdown` is optional and can be omitted. The default behavior in this case: `SIGTERM` is issued to the process group of the running process.

In case only `shutdown.signal` is defined `[1..31]` the running process group will be terminated with its value.

If `shutdown.parent_only` is yes, the signal is only sent to the running process and not to the whole process group.

In case the `shutdown.command` is defined:

1. The `shutdown.command` is executed with all the Environment Variables of the primary process
2. Wait for `shutdown.timeout_seconds` for its completion (if not defined wait for 10 seconds)
3. In case of timeout, the process group will receive the `SIGKILL` signal (irrespective of the `shutdown.parent_only` option).

The `shutdown.command` is [rendered](configuration.md#variables) like the `command` is, so it can use `{{.PC_REPLICA_NUM}}` and your own `vars`:

```yaml hl_lines="6"
processes:
  server:
    command: "python3 -m http.server 404{{.PC_REPLICA_NUM}}"
    replicas: 2
    shutdown:
      command: "curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:404{{.PC_REPLICA_NUM}}/quit"
```

> :bulb: If your shutdown command contains literal Go template syntax (`docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}'`, `kubectl -o go-template`), [escape it](configuration.md#template-escaping) or set `is_template_disabled: true` on the process.

In case the `shutdown.timeout_seconds` is defined (without `shutdown.command`) and the process will fail to terminate within that time, the process group will receive the `SIGKILL` signal.

### Stopping Interactive Processes With Keystrokes

Some tty/console programs exit only on a keystroke (e.g. `q`) and ignore termination signals. For these, `shutdown.send_keys` writes the configured keys to the process's stdin to trigger a clean, key-based shutdown. It requires `is_interactive: true` (or `is_tty: true`).

```yaml
processes:
  viewer:
    command: "less /var/log/syslog"
    is_interactive: true
    shutdown:
      send_keys: "q"        # written to the process's stdin on stop
      timeout_seconds: 10   # default 10
```

When `shutdown.send_keys` is defined (and `shutdown.command` is not):

1. The interpreted keys are written to the running process's stdin.
2. Wait for `shutdown.timeout_seconds` for the process to exit (if not defined wait for 10 seconds).
3. In case of timeout, the process group will receive the `SIGKILL` signal.

Control keys can be expressed with escape sequences: `\xHH` (hex, e.g. `\x03` for `Ctrl-C`), `\r`, `\n`, `\t`, `\e` (ESC), `\0` (NUL), `\\`, and the usual `\a \b \f \v`. No trailing newline is added, so add `\r` yourself if the program needs `Enter` to submit (e.g. `send_keys: 'q\r'`).

- `depends_on` conditions of type `process_completed_successfully` are satisfied.
- The project's own exit code is `0`.

`0` is always a success and never needs to be listed. Codes must be in the range `0-255`.

```yaml hl_lines="4"
processes:
  nginx:
    command: "docker run -d --rm --name nginx_test nginx" # note the '-d' for detached mode
    is_daemon: true # this flag is required for background processes (default false)
    launch_timeout_seconds: 2 # default 5s
    shutdown:
      command: "docker stop nginx_test"
      timeout_seconds: 10 # default 10
      signal: 15 # default 15, but only if command is not defined or empty
```

1. For processes that start services / daemons in the background, please use the `is_daemon` flag set to `true`.

2. In case a process is daemon it will be considered running until stopped.

3. Daemon processes can only be stopped with the `$PROCESSNAME.shutdown.command` as in the example above.

4. If parent process (starter) won’t close `stdout` and `stderr` within specified `launch_timeout_seconds`, (default 5 seconds) process compose will stop waiting for its log completion and start waiting for process termination. ## Successful Exit Codes

By default only exit code `0` is considered a success; any other code marks the process as `Failed`. When `process-compose` terminates a process with a signal, the process exits with the UNIX convention `128 + signal` — for example `130` for `SIGINT` (signal 2) or `143` for `SIGTERM` (signal 15).     success_exit_codes: [130] # 130 == 128 + SIGINT, treated as a clean exit

- `depends_on` conditions of type `process_completed_successfully` are satisfied.

# Release Notes

## Unreleased

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed concurrent probe shutdowns panicking with `close of closed channel`. Probe starts and stops are now serialized, and a pending initial-delay start cannot revive a stopped or superseded probe.

## [v1.124.0] - 2026-10-27

### New Features

- Extended [template rendering](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/configuration/#rendered-parameters) to more process fields: `entrypoint`, `shutdown.command`, `ready_log_line`, `env_file`, `log_configuration.rotation.directory` and `filename`, the exec probe `working_dir`, and HTTP probe `headers`. A template that fails to render now names the process and the field it came from. [`is_template_disabled`](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/configuration/#disable-command-rendering) now covers `entrypoint` and `shutdown.command` along with `command`, so a shutdown command or entrypoint with literal Go template syntax (e.g. `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}'`) needs [escaping](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/configuration/#template-escaping) or that flag.
- Added `PC_CLIENT_LOG_FILE` to set the [log file of client commands](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/logging/#client-commands-and-pc_log_file). Client commands no longer share the server's `PC_LOG_FILE` path (truncating the server's log on every call): they now log to a `-client` sibling of it, e.g. `pc.log` becomes `pc-client.log`.

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed processes with a [`schedule`](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/scheduled-processes/) that were added or changed by a project update or reload running once immediately and never being scheduled. They are now registered as they are at startup (a disabled one stays paused), a schedule change alone triggers the update, and a removed or replaced process no longer leaves its old schedule behind, addresses issue #561, by @jihtsan.
- Fixed a `process_healthy` dependent being skipped when it started while its still-running dependency was temporarily not ready after a nonfatal [readiness probe](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/health/#readiness-probe) failure, which also stamped the dependency with `exit_code=1`. The dependent now waits for the dependency to become ready again, addresses issue #544.
- Fixed the first [`project update`](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/cli/process-compose_project_update/) after a server start restarting every process even when its configuration had not changed.
- Fixed replicas of a scaled process sharing one copy of their probes and log rotation settings, so every replica used the values rendered for the first one: the documented readiness probe with [`port: "404{{.PC_REPLICA_NUM}}"`](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/configuration/#auto-inserted-variables) probed replica 0's port from every replica.
- Fixed several log streaming issues: in `attach` mode a process whose log was not being followed showed an empty log pane, log backlogs larger than 256 lines sent over the API were mostly dropped, a log request for several processes ended all of them when the first one finished, and a line written while a viewer subscribed could be shown twice or not at all, addresses issue #539.
- Fixed [`process-compose process logs`](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/cli/process-compose_process_logs/) without `--follow` printing a spurious `write close: ... broken pipe` error on stderr after a successful run, by @emeka.
- Fixed CJK and other wide characters being garbled in the terminal view of [interactive processes](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/interactive-processes/), where each character overwrote the right half of the wide character before it, addresses issue #535.
- Fixed the TUI process table reshuffling stopped processes on every refresh when sorted by CPU or memory, and the selection jumping to a different process when a refresh reordered the rows. Ties now sort by name, and the column chosen with `--sort` is marked in the header from the start, addresses issue #547.
- Client commands no longer check GitHub for a newer release, since scripts running them in a loop could exhaust the machine's unauthenticated GitHub API rate limit. The remaining update checks identify themselves with a `process-compose/<version>` User-Agent, addresses issue #552.
- Fixed `environment` entries whose value contains `=` (e.g. `DSN=host=db user=app`) being dropped when [merging configuration files](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/merge/#adding-and-overriding-configuration) or using [`extends`](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/merge/#process-inheritance-with-extends), by @bensynapse.
- Fixed the Swagger UI always targeting `localhost:8080` when the [API server](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/client/#rest-api) runs on a different address or port, by @icyleaf.
- Fixed the [REST API](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/client/#rest-api) returning a process `namespace` as a plain string when it holds a single namespace, while the OpenAPI spec declares an array of strings, which broke clients generated from the spec. `namespace` is now always an array in JSON output (REST responses, the process state WebSocket, and `process list`, `process get` and `process monitor` with `-o json`). Requests and YAML configs still accept a plain string. Anything that expects a string needs updating, including scripts that compare `namespace` to a string and process-compose client binaries older than v1.122.0, addresses issue #538.

---

## [v1.122.0] - 2026-08-18

### New Features

- Added [file watching](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/watch/): a per-process `watch` block restarts a process when its files change, with include/exclude globs, a configurable `debounce`, and `cascade: true` to restart the process's dependents transitively (in dependency order, so a rebuilt artifact is ready before its consumers restart). A process that has exited while its watch is still armed reports the new `Watching` state, and the TUI names the file that caused each restart. Watch-triggered restarts skip the restart backoff and reset the restart counter, since they are user intent rather than a crash loop. File watching can be turned off entirely with `--no-watch` / `PC_NO_WATCH`.
- Added support for [multiple namespaces per process](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/configuration/#multiple-namespaces): `namespace` now accepts either a single string or a list of strings (similar to docker-compose profiles), so a shared process (e.g. a database) can be selected and operated as part of any of its namespaces, addresses issue #519.

### Bug Fixes

7:Process Compose can restart a process when its source files change, and - with `cascade` - restart everything that depends on it. This replaces wrapping each command in a per-language watcher (`air`, `nodemon`, `watchexec`, `cargo-watch`).
9:Wrapping has a cost that is easy to miss: the wrapper becomes the process Process Compose manages, so `shutdown.signal`, `success_exit_codes` and PTY handling apply to the wrapper rather than to your program, `liveness_probe` measures the wrapper's lifetime (it never dies, so a crash-looping app looks healthy), and the `Restarts` counter never moves. A built-in watch keeps all of those pointed at the real process - and, unlike any per-language watcher, it knows your dependency graph.
26:Saving anything under `./src` restarts `api`, except test files.
33:| `debounce` | string | `300ms` | Go duration to let a burst of changes settle before restarting |
34:| `cascade` | bool | false | Also restart this process's dependents, transitively |
44:| `include` | list | - | If set, only matching files trigger a restart |
62:## Cascading Restarts
64:`cascade: true` restarts the watched process and then everything that depends on it, in dependency order.
71:      restart: "no"                    # one-shot
87:- Editing `./assets/app.scss` re-runs `make assets`, **then** restarts `api`.
88:- Editing `./src/main.go` restarts `api` alone.
91:> Restarts propagate **downstream to dependents, never upstream to dependencies**. A change to `api` will not re-run `assets`. If a change should rebuild an artifact and then restart its consumers, put the watch on the process that produces the artifact and set `cascade: true` there.
99:The TUI also reports each watch-triggered restart in the status bar, naming the file that caused it. Bursts are folded into a single summary so that rapid restarts stay readable.
113:The classic trap is a process that writes into a directory it also watches, so each restart triggers the next. The default excludes cover the usual build output directories, but if a loop does occur Process Compose detects it, logs an error naming the process and the file that triggered it, and suspends that watch until the project is reloaded rather than looping forever.
123:| `replicas > 1` | Each replica would install its own watcher on the same tree, multiplying descriptors and restarts |
124:| `schedule` | A restart does not reschedule the cron job, and scheduler concurrency limits would not see watch-driven starts |
53:  # Older versions (<= v1.110.0) require the dependencies to be manually expanded
328:1. Foreground process have to be started manually (`F7`). They can be started multiple times.
344:Even if disabled, the process is still listed in the TUI and the REST client, and can be started manually when needed.
346:## Auto Restart on Exit
353:      backoff_seconds: 2 # default: 1
    command: "ls -R /"
    disabled: true #default false
```

Even if disabled, the process is still listed in the TUI and the REST client, and can be started manually when needed.

## Auto Restart on Exit

```yaml hl_lines="4"
processes:
  process2:
    availability:
      restart: on_failure # other options: "exit_on_failure", "always", "no" (default)
      backoff_seconds: 2 # default: 1
      max_restarts: 5 # default: 0 (unlimited)
```

## Terminate Process Compose on Failure

## Process State

A process that has exited **successfully** but still has an armed watch reports the **`Watching`** state rather than `Completed`, in the TUI, in `process-compose process list` and over the REST API. It signals that the process is waiting for a file to change - and explains why the project is still running.

A process that failed keeps `Failed` or `Error`. `Watching` never stands in for a failure: a broken build is the most important thing a watch loop has to report, and the watch stays armed either way, so the next save still triggers a rebuild.

The TUI also reports each watch-triggered restart in the status bar, naming the file that caused it. Bursts are folded into a single summary so that rapid restarts stay readable.

## Project Lifetime

While any watch is armed, the project stays up even after every process has exited - otherwise a project of one-shot builders would exit before a watch could ever fire.

Stopping a process pauses its watch, so a stopped process is never brought back by a file change. Starting it again resumes the watch.

This works on a process that has already exited: stopping something in the `Watching` state disarms its watch, which is how you leave that state. The process drops back to `Completed`, and if nothing else is running or armed the project then finishes.

To run without watching at all - in CI, or in a script - use `--no-watch` (or `PC_NO_WATCH`). Then `up` behaves exactly as it did before watching existed, `watch` blocks are ignored, and the project exits when its processes finish.

## Feedback Loops

        condition: process_completed_successfully
```

## Terminate Process Compose once given process ends

There are cases when you might want `process-compose` to terminate immediately when one of the processes exits (regardless of the exit code). For example when running tests that depend on other processes like databases etc. You might want the processes, on which the test process depends, to start first, then run the tests, and finally terminate all processes once the test process exits, reporting the code returned by the test process.

To achieve that, set `availability.exit_on_end` to `true`, and `process-compose` will gracefully shut down all the other running processes and exit with the same exit code as the given process.

```yaml hl_lines="7"
processes:
  tests:
    command: tests-run
    availability:
      # NOTE: `restart: exit_on_failure` is not needed since
      # exit_on_end implies it.
      exit_on_end: true
    depends_on:
      redis:
        condition: process_healthy
      postgres:
        condition: process_healthy

  redis:
    command: redis-start
    readiness_probe:
      exec:
        command: redis-health-check

  postgres:
    command: postgres-start
    readiness_probe:
      exec:
        command: postgres-health-check
```

> :bulb:
> setting `restart: exit_on_failure` together with `exit_on_end: true` is not needed as the latter causes termination regardless of the exit code. However, it might be sometimes useful to `exit_on_end` with `restart: on_failure` and `max_restarts` in case you want the process to recover from failure and only cause termination on success.

> :bulb:
> `exit_on_end` can be set on more than one process, for example when running multiple tasks in parallel and wishing to terminate as soon as any one finished.

## Terminate Process Compose once given process is skipped

### When Is a Process Stopped

A process is stopped once its **whole process group** is gone, not when the command itself exits. The two are often far apart: a shell wrapper (`npm run dev`, `cd app && ./server`, a launcher script) dies the instant the signal arrives, while the server behind it is still draining connections and holding its port. Until the group is empty the process stays in the `Terminating` state.

This is what makes a restart safe. Restarting a process - manually, on a [file change](watch.md), or by a project update - launches the new instance only after the old one is gone, so the two never compete for the same port:

1. The process is stopped as described above.
2. Process Compose waits for the process group to exit.
3. The new instance is launched (after `backoff_seconds`, for a manual restart).

How long step 2 may take is yours to decide:

- With `shutdown.timeout_seconds` set, whatever is left of the process group is killed with `SIGKILL` when the timeout expires, and the restart proceeds.
- Without it, a command that does not exit is never killed, and a restart waits for it for as long as it takes (a warning is logged every 10 seconds). If the command has exited but other members of its group linger, they are given 10 seconds before the process is reported as stopped anyway, with a warning.

A migration script that leaves a helper running is `Completed` when the script ends, and the processes waiting for it with `process_completed` or `process_completed_successfully` start right away.
''')

> :bulb:

new='''The TUI also reports each watch-triggered restart in the status bar, naming the file that caused it. Bursts are folded into a single summary so that rapid restarts stay readable.

See [When Is a Process Stopped](launcher.md#when-is-a-process-stopped) for how long that may take and how to bound it with `shutdown.timeout_seconds`.
'''
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='docs/release-notes.md'
s=open(p).read()
old='''- Fixed concurrent probe shutdowns panicking with `close of closed channel`. Probe starts and stops are now serialized, and a pending initial-delay start cannot revive a stopped or superseded probe.
'''
new=old+'''- Fixed a restarted process failing with `address already in use` (or otherwise colliding with itself) because the new instance was launched while the old one was still shutting down. This hit [file-watch](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/watch/) restarts in particular, which skip the restart backoff that used to hide it. A restart now waits until the old instance - its [whole process group](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/launcher/#when-is-a-process-stopped), not just a shell wrapper in front of the real server - has exited. For the same reason a stopped process now stays `Terminating` until its process group is gone, and with `shutdown.timeout_seconds` set, group members that outlive the command are killed at the timeout as documented. Without a timeout a process that ignores its stop signal is never killed, so a restart now waits for it instead of starting a second copy next to it.
- Fixed a process that had exited still showing as `Running`, and its `process_completed` / `process_completed_successfully` dependents never starting, when something it started in the background kept its `stdout` or `stderr` open (a migration script launching a helper, `pg_ctl start` without a log file). A process now completes when its command exits. The output of whatever it left behind is still captured.
- Fixed `process-compose` exiting with `255` instead of the exit code of the process that ended the project. With more than one process carrying `exit_on_end` or `exit_on_failure`, the ones terminated by the shutdown overwrote the exit code of the process that caused it - so a failing test run reported `255` rather than its own code, and so did a passing one. The first process to end the project now decides its exit code, and a shutdown requested with `Ctrl+C` or `process-compose down` exits with `0`.
- Fixed processes terminated by a signal reporting exit code `-1`. They now report `128 + signal` (`143` for `SIGTERM`, `137` for `SIGKILL`), as [documented](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/launcher/#successful-exit-codes), which also makes such exits matchable by `success_exit_codes`. Anything that compares a process `exit_code` to `-1` needs updating.
- Fixed a process being killed shortly after it was restarted by a failed readiness probe when `shutdown.timeout_seconds` was set: the `SIGKILL` armed for the instance being stopped was delivered to its replacement once the timeout expired.
- Fixed a process that was stopped, or restarted, at the very moment it was being launched starting anyway, and one that ended at the very moment it was stopped being left in `Terminating`.
- Fixed a process launched while the project was shutting down - by an in-flight restart or a schedule - being left running after `process-compose` had exited.
- The TUI no longer freezes while a process is being restarted with the restart shortcut.
'''
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

content.text:
All three problems are fixed. Each one reproduced on the unmodified binary and no longer does. The full race suite, lint, and macOS/Windows cross-builds pass; I only ran it on Linux. Nothing is committed.

## What was wrong

- **"Address already in use" on save.** A restart sent the stop signal and launched the replacement straight away. Manual restarts were mostly hidden by the 1-second backoff, but file-watch restarts skip backoff. Now a restart waits until the old instance has exited, including its whole process group, so a shell wrapper (`npm run dev`, `cd x && ./server`) dying first no longer counts as stopped.
- **`migrate` stuck on Running.** Process-compose waited for the process's stdout to close before noticing it had exited. If the script left anything in the background holding stdout, that never happened. Now a process is complete when its command exits; output from whatever it left behind is still captured.
- **255 / -1 in CI.** Two causes:
  - When one process ended the project, every other process killed by the shutdown that also had `exit_on_failure` or `exit_on_end` overwrote the exit code. Even a passing test run exited 255. Now the first process to end the project decides the code.
  - A signal-killed process reported `-1`; it now reports `128 + signal` (143, 137), as the docs already claimed.

## Related fixes in the same paths

- With `shutdown.timeout_seconds` set, a process restarted by a failed readiness probe had its replacement SIGKILLed when the old instance's timeout expired.
- A stop that arrived just as a process was launching could be lost, and one that arrived just as it ended could leave it stuck in `Terminating`.
- A restart or schedule firing during project shutdown could leave a process running after process-compose exited.
- The per-process log file writer could crash with "send on closed channel"; the stdout change would have made that easier to hit.
- The TUI restart shortcut ran on the UI thread and would have frozen the UI during the new wait, so it is now asynchronous.

## Behaviour changes you'll notice

- Anything comparing a process `exit_code` to `-1` needs updating.
- `Ctrl+C` or `process-compose down` now exits `0` even when the stack has `exit_on_failure` services; it used to exit 255.
- A stopped process stays `Terminating` until its process group is gone.
- A restart of a process that ignores its stop signal and has no `shutdown.timeout_seconds` now waits, logging a warning every 10 seconds, instead of starting a second copy beside it. Set `shutdown.timeout_seconds` on anything that might not exit promptly.
- A daemon (`is_daemon`) with no `shutdown.command` now shows as stopped once it has been signalled, rather than sitting in `Terminating` forever.

The new regression tests fail against the original code, apart from a few guard tests that only compile against the new code. The engine changes are in `src/app/process.go`, `src/app/project_runner.go` and `src/command/`; the docs (`www/docs/launcher.md`, `www/docs/watch.md`) and release notes are updated.

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='docs/release-notes.md'
s=open(p).read()
old='''- Fixed processes terminated by a signal reporting exit code `-1`.'''
new='''- Fixed `process-compose run` terminating itself and the script that called it (`Terminated`, exit `143`) when the project shut down while the foreground process was still running, for instance because a dependency with `exit_on_failure` had failed. The caller never received the exit code and never reached its own clean-up. The foreground process shares the process group of `process-compose`, and stopping it signalled that whole group; it and its child processes are now signalled individually. The same applied to stopping an elevated process without the TUI.
- Fixed processes terminated by a signal reporting exit code `-1`.'''
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='www/docs/launcher.md'
s=open(p).read()
old='''Where the process group is not signalled, only the command itself is waited for:'''
new='''The foreground process of [`process-compose run`](cli/process-compose_run.md) is the one process without a group of its own: it shares the process group of `process-compose` itself so that it keeps the terminal. Stopping it signals the process and its child processes individually, never that group - `process-compose` and the script that launched it are left alone, and the script receives the project's exit code.

Where the process group is not signalled, only the command itself is waited for:'''
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
ls www/docs/cli/process-compose_run.md && GOOS=darwin go vet ./src/command/ ./src/app/ && GOOS=windows go vet ./src/command/ ./src/app/ && make lint 2>&1 | tail -2 && go test -race -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | grep -v "no test files" | tail -20

content.text:
Fixed: your script now gets the real exit code and runs its clean-up. With `db` exiting 4 under `process-compose run tests`, the script prints its clean-up line and exits `4`; before, on both the original binary and my first round of changes, it died with `Terminated` / 143.

## Cause

`run` starts its foreground process (`tests`) in process-compose's own process group so that it keeps the terminal. Stopping a process signals its process group. When `db` failed and the project shut down, stopping `tests` sent SIGTERM to that shared group, which contains process-compose and the shell script that launched it.

This was already wrong before my changes, and I missed it: I saw the shared group while reworking the stop path and left it as existing behaviour, and I only tested `up`, never `run`.

## Fix

A process that shares process-compose's group is now stopped by signalling it and its child processes individually, never the group. The same bug affected stopping an elevated process without the TUI and is fixed by the same change.

## Checked

- Your scenario, from a shell script: exit `4`, clean-up runs, and the test process's own child is stopped rather than left behind.
- `tests` failing with 3 gives `3`; `tests` passing gives `0`; clean-up runs in both.
- Two new regression tests fail (process killed by SIGTERM) when the old group signal is put back.
- Full race suite and lint pass; macOS and Windows cross-builds pass.

Not checked: `run` from an interactive terminal (Ctrl+C handling). The macOS code for finding child processes compiles but was not run. Docs and release notes are updated; still nothing committed.

In the first round I made a signal-based stop of a daemon count as "stopped" so its stop would complete — but a real daemon like redis detaches from the launcher's process group, so the signal reaches nobody and I was reporting success for something I never touched. Reproducing, then fixing it so a daemon only reads Completed when it is verifiably gone.

content.text:
Fixed. `process-compose process stop redis` fails again for a detached daemon, and redis is shown as `Launched`, because it is still running.

That regression was mine. In the first round I made a signal-based stop of a daemon count as "stopped" so the stop would finish. For a daemon like redis that detaches from its launcher, the signal reaches nothing, so I was reporting success for a process I never touched.

## What happens now

For an `is_daemon` process with no `shutdown.command`:

- **Daemon has detached (your redis):**
  - Stop fails with exit code 1. Add `-v` to see the reason; without it the CLI only prints `Failed to stop: 'redis'`:
    ```
    ✘ Failed to stop redis: cannot be stopped by a signal: daemon redis is no longer in the process group of the command that launched it, and is still running. Define shutdown.command to stop it
    ```
  - The state stays `Launched`. The original left it stuck in `Terminating`.
  - Restart fails the same way rather than launching a second redis.
  - `process-compose down` leaves it running with a warning in the log and exits. On the original, `down` after a failed stop hung.
- **Daemon still in the launcher's process group:** it is signalled, and only shown `Completed` once it has actually exited. With `shutdown.timeout_seconds` it is killed at the timeout; without one it stays `Terminating` until it is gone.

Process-compose still cannot stop your redis itself. To make stop, restart and `down` work, give it a shutdown command:

```yaml
redis:
  is_daemon: true
  shutdown:
    command: "redis-cli shutdown"
```

## Checked

- **Your case via the CLI**, with a stand-in daemon that detaches the way redis does: stop fails, state is `Launched`, the port is still held, and `down` returns.
- **In-group daemon via the CLI:** stop succeeds and the port is released.
- **Regression tests:** new tests cover both daemon cases, including restart and project shutdown.
- **Suite:** the full race suite and lint pass; macOS and Windows builds compile.

On Windows a launched daemon without `shutdown.command` is now always treated as unreachable, so its stop fails; I have not run that there. Docs and release notes are updated. Nothing is committed.

old='''> :bulb: `STDIN` and `Windows` are not supported at this time.

A process with `is_tty` is [stopped](launcher.md#termination-parameters) like any other process: it receives the configured `shutdown.signal` (`SIGTERM` by default), whatever it writes while shutting down is captured in its log, and it reports its own exit code. Its terminal is closed only after it has exited.

This differs from [interactive processes](interactive-processes.md) (`is_interactive`), which are terminal sessions and are ended by hanging up: `SIGTERM` is replaced by `SIGHUP` and the terminal is closed at once.
'''
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='docs/release-notes.md'
s=open(p).read()
old='''- Fixed processes terminated by a signal reporting exit code `-1`.'''
new='''- Fixed stopping or restarting a process with [`is_tty`](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/configuration/#pseudo-terminals) cutting off its log at the stop signal and corrupting its exit code. Its terminal was closed the moment the signal was sent, so everything it wrote while shutting down was lost and failed to write - which is why a program that exited cleanly could be reported with a code such as `120`, the status some runtimes use for a failed flush at exit. It was also sent `SIGHUP` in place of the configured `SIGTERM`. Such a process is now stopped like any other: it gets the configured signal, its shutdown output is logged, and it reports its own exit code. A tty process that relied on being hung up - one that ignores `SIGTERM` - needs `shutdown.signal: 1` or `shutdown.timeout_seconds`. Interactive processes (`is_interactive`) are still ended by hanging up.
- Fixed processes terminated by a signal reporting exit code `-1`.'''
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

content.text:
Fixed: an `is_tty` process now logs its whole shutdown, exits with its own status, and receives the configured signal. My stand-in front end went from one shutdown line and exit `120` to all its shutdown lines, exit `0`, and `SIGTERM`.

## Cause

Stopping a process that runs on a terminal did three things meant for interactive sessions, and applied them to `is_tty` as well:

- **It closed the terminal the instant the signal was sent.** Every write after that failed, so the shutdown output was lost. In my Python stand-in, `120` is the runtime's status for a failed flush of stdout at exit, so the program really did return it, but only because its terminal had been taken away.
- **It started a second reader that discarded the terminal's output**, competing with the log.
- **It replaced `SIGTERM` with `SIGHUP`**, so your front end was never sent the signal you configured.

All three are in the original code. I saw the terminal being closed on stop in the first round and left it alone; for `is_tty` that was wrong.

## Fix

An `is_tty` process is now stopped like any other process, and its terminal is closed only after it has exited and its output has been read. `is_interactive` processes are unchanged: they are still ended by hanging up.

## One behaviour change

An `is_tty` process that ignores `SIGTERM` used to die anyway because it was hung up. It now needs `shutdown.signal: 1` or `shutdown.timeout_seconds`.

## Checked

- **Your case via the CLI:** stop and restart of a tty process give full shutdown output and exit `0`.
- **Interactive shell:** still stops, with exit 129 from the hangup.
- **Regression tests:** new tests fail with the old behaviour restored.
- **Suite:** full race suite and lint pass; macOS and Windows builds compile.

One thing I noticed and did not change: sending an arbitrary signal to an `is_interactive` process (the TUI signal menu or the API) also closes its terminal, because it goes through the same code as stop. Say if you want that fixed too.

Docs and release notes are updated. Nothing is committed.

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='www/docs/launcher.md'
s=open(p).read()
old='''## Successful Exit Codes
'''
new='''### Stopping Process Compose Itself

Process Compose stops its processes, as described above, before it exits. In headless mode (`-t=false`, `run`, detached) that happens on any of:

| Trigger | Typical source |
|---------|----------------|
| `SIGINT` | `Ctrl+C` |
| `SIGQUIT` | `Ctrl+\\` |
| `SIGTERM` | `kill`, a CI runner or supervisor |
| `SIGHUP` | the terminal being closed |
| its output being closed | `process-compose up -t=false \\| head`, or a log collector that exits |

All of them start the same graceful shutdown, and `process-compose` exits with `0` once every process is gone.

A graceful shutdown waits for every process, so a process that ignores its stop signal and has no `shutdown.timeout_seconds` holds it up indefinitely. **Sending a second signal** - pressing `Ctrl+C` or `Ctrl+\\` again, at least a second after the first - forces the matter: every process group is killed with `SIGKILL`, and `process-compose` exits with `128 + signal` (`130` for `SIGINT`, `131` for `SIGQUIT`). Signals that arrive together with the first one are treated as part of the same request, so a supervisor sending `SIGTERM` and `SIGHUP` at once still gets a graceful shutdown.

> :bulb: `kill -9` (`SIGKILL`) cannot be handled by any program. If Process Compose is killed that way, its processes keep running; stop it with a signal it can act on instead. For a goroutine dump of a hung Process Compose - what `SIGQUIT` used to produce - send `SIGABRT`.

## Successful Exit Codes
'''
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='docs/release-notes.md'
s=open(p).read()
old='''- Fixed stopping or restarting a process with [`is_tty`]'''
new='''- Fixed `process-compose` leaving all of its processes running, ports included, when it was ended by `SIGQUIT` (`Ctrl+\\`) - which also printed a dump of every goroutine - or by its output being closed (`process-compose up -t=false | head`). Both now [shut the processes down first](https://f1bonacc1.github.io/process-compose/launcher/#stopping-process-compose-itself), like `Ctrl+C` does. For a goroutine dump, send `SIGABRT`.
- A second signal during a shutdown now forces it: the remaining processes are killed with `SIGKILL` and `process-compose` exits with `128 + signal`. Previously further signals were ignored, so a shutdown held up by a process that ignores its stop signal could only be escaped by killing `process-compose` itself, leaving that process and any others behind. Signals delivered together with the first one do not count.
- Fixed stopping or restarting a process with [`is_tty`]'''
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

content.text:
Fixed. Ctrl-\ now shuts everything down the way Ctrl-C does: no stack trace, exit `0`, and `api` and `worker` are gone with their ports released.

## Cause

Process-compose handled SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP but not SIGQUIT, which is what Ctrl-\ sends. Unhandled, the Go runtime dumps every goroutine and exits on the spot. Each managed process runs in its own process group, so the terminal's signal never reaches them and nothing stopped them. This is in the original code too.

## What changed

- **Ctrl-\ (SIGQUIT)** starts the normal graceful shutdown.
- **A second signal forces it.** Making Ctrl-\ graceful would otherwise remove your only way out of a shutdown that hangs on a process ignoring its stop signal. So a second Ctrl-C or Ctrl-\ now kills every remaining process group and exits with `128 + signal` (130 or 131). It has to come at least a second after the first, so a supervisor sending SIGTERM and SIGHUP together still gets a graceful shutdown.
- **Closed output pipe.** While checking for the same failure by other routes I found one more: `process-compose up -t=false | head` was killed by SIGPIPE when the reader exited and left the processes running. It now shuts down cleanly. An API client disconnecting does not trigger it.

## Things to know

- `kill -9` on process-compose still leaves its processes running; no program can handle that signal.
- SIGQUIT no longer prints a goroutine dump. Send SIGABRT if you need one from a hung process-compose.
- `go.mod` now lists `golang.org/x/sys` as a direct dependency, at the same version; the vendored tree is byte-identical, so the Nix hash is unaffected.

## Checked

- **End to end, headless:** SIGQUIT, SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP each exit `0` with nothing left running.
- **Forced path:** with a worker that ignores SIGTERM, the first signal waits, the second kills it and exits `131`.
- **Pipe case:** `| head -2` exits cleanly with nothing left.
- **Tests:** new unit tests for the signal handling and the forced shutdown; full race suite and lint pass; macOS and Windows builds compile.

Not checked: the TUI path. I added SIGQUIT to its handler, but did not run it in a real terminal; there Ctrl-\ arrives as a keystroke, so only an external `kill -QUIT` reaches it.

Docs and release notes are updated. Nothing is committed.
